Data Destruction and Chain-of-Custody Policy

How Spano Technologies LLC handles every computer and storage device it collects from a business: who touches it, where it is kept, how its data is destroyed, and what record the client receives.

Version 1.3, effective November 27, 2026. Spano Technologies LLC, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Download the signed-off PDF.

  • Logged. Every device by serial number on a signed transfer of ownership.
  • Locked. Removed drives kept in a locked case until shredding.
  • Shredded. By Elemental Inc., an R2v3-certified recycler in Philadelphia.
  • Certified. A certificate listing every device and drive within 15 business days.

Scope

This policy covers every laptop, desktop, phone, tablet and storage device collected by Spano Technologies LLC from a business client, and the drives inside them, from the moment the transfer of ownership is signed until the storage is destroyed or erased and the device is resold or recycled.

We do not accept equipment from medical, dental or other offices holding patient records (protected health information), and we do not sign business associate agreements.

Who handles equipment

Cole Spano, the company's owner, personally handles every client device from pickup to final disposition. No employees or subcontractors handle client equipment. The only other party is our recycler, Elemental Inc. (2371 Church St, Philadelphia; R2v3 certificate C2026-03761), which shreds drives and recycles what cannot be reused. The recycler receives drives and drive serial numbers, never client names.

Before the pickup

We confirm the office is eligible, agree the device count and a pickup time, and put any per-unit offer in writing before we come. We ask the client to:

  • back up anything they want to keep: once a drive is shredded, nothing on it can be returned;
  • release devices from device management and locks (Windows Autopilot and Intune, Apple Business Manager and Activation Lock, the Google account on Android phones and tablets, Absolute, BIOS passwords);
  • tell us whether their policy allows built-in storage to be erased, or requires it to be physically destroyed.

At the pickup

Every device is recorded by type, make and model, serial number and asset tag on a Transfer of Ownership, signed by an authorized representative of the client and by Spano Technologies LLC. Each device gets a label with the pickup number and its line on the form, so the paperwork and the machine always match. The client receives a copy of the signed form, by email before we leave when it is signed on screen, or on paper.

Serial numbers are recorded with our own phone app, which reads each one from the device's label and keeps a photo of that label. The owner checks every serial against the label itself before moving on to the next device. Where a drive is easy to reach, its serial number is recorded the same way at the pickup and listed on the form; otherwise it is recorded when the drive is removed (section 05). Label photos show only the outside of the device or drive, never a screen.

Nobody opens a client's operating system or files. A device is powered on only to its firmware screens (to read serial numbers and lock status), or after its storage has been removed or erased. Phones and tablets are never unlocked or browsed: each is identified by the serial number or IMEI on the device, its SIM tray or its box. SIM cards are handed back to the client at the pickup, and memory cards go into the pickup's drive envelope.

Transport and storage

Equipment travels in closed containers, out of sight, and is taken directly to our storage after the pickup. It is never left in an unattended vehicle overnight. Storage is private, locked and not open to the public.

Removable drives are taken out and their serial numbers recorded against their device in our pickup log before any other work is done, and checked against the serial recorded at the pickup where there is one. Each pickup's drives go into one envelope marked with the pickup number, date and drive count, kept in a locked case until the recycler run. Only the owner holds the key.

Destruction methods

Removable drives (hard drives, SATA and NVMe SSDs), and any memory cards, USB drives or loose drives the client hands over, are physically shredded by Elemental. We record each drive's serial number, and Elemental records it again at shredding, so every drive on the certificate is matched to the recycler's own serial record and its shredding receipt.

Built-in storage that cannot be removed (most MacBooks, phones and tablets, for example) is erased with the maker's own erase function, only where the client's policy allows it: on a Mac, iPhone or iPad, Erase All Content and Settings, which discards the storage encryption keys; on an Android phone or tablet that launched with Android 10 or later (encrypted by default), a factory reset, which discards its encryption keys. The result is checked and photographed. If the client requires physical destruction, or the device cannot be erased (it is locked, does not work, or is an Android model that launched before Android 10), the whole device goes to Elemental for shredding.

Spano Technologies LLC is not itself a certified disposal facility and claims no certification or standard of its own. Shredding is done by our R2v3-certified recycler.

Reuse and recycling

A device is refurbished or resold only after its storage has been destroyed or erased. Asset tags, stickers and anything else that identifies the client come off first, and the client's name never appears in any listing. A device still locked after the client's release window may be sold for parts or recycled, and its storage is destroyed either way. Everything that cannot be reused goes to Elemental for recycling, never to a landfill.

The certificate

Within 15 business days of the pickup, the client receives a signed Certificate of Data Destruction listing every device by serial number and asset tag, every drive by serial number, how its storage was handled, the date, who checked it, and the recycler's receipt number for shredded drives.

Records and privacy

The signed transfer, the pickup log, the label photos, the certificate and the recycler's receipts are kept for at least three years. A client's contact details are used only to arrange the pickup and send its paperwork. They are never sold or shared.

While a pickup is in progress, its record (the client's contact details, serial numbers, label photos and signatures) is kept inside our app on the owner's phone, which is locked with a passcode and Face ID. The app keeps it encrypted, out of the phone's photo library and out of cloud backups, and never sends it to any outside service; the only thing it sends is the signed transfer, by email to the client. The record is copied to the company's own files, then deleted from the phone.

If something goes wrong

If a device or drive cannot be accounted for, or is damaged before its storage is destroyed, we tell the client in writing within two business days of finding out, with what happened and what we are doing about it.

Questions and review

Questions about this policy or any pickup: info@spanotechnologies.com or (484) 957-1712. This policy is reviewed every year and whenever the process changes; the version and date are at the top.
